subtype: Toddler who does not seek comfort [Actor]
passage:
"Bye, Uday. Amma's going to the market." Hansa waves at the door.
Uday doesn't look up from his stacking cups.
"He didn't even cry," Dadi says.
"He never does," Hansa says, and goes.
Later Uday bumps his head on the table. His lip trembles. He turns to the wall and pats the floor, alone.
Hansa comes home. "Oof, a bump? Come, raja."
Uday stays by the wall, very still.
"Maybe quiet doesn't mean fine," Dadi says softly.

qa.q: What was Uday playing with when Hansa left?
qa.a: He was playing with his stacking cups.

qa.q: What does Uday's trembling lip suggest after he bumps his head?
qa.a: It suggests he is hurt and upset, even though he turns to the wall instead of looking for comfort.

qa.q: What could Hansa try when Uday stays by the wall?
qa.a: She could sit near him quietly and offer comfort gently without forcing it, so he learns that showing need brings care.

qa.q: How does Dadi's view of Uday change by the end?
qa.a: At first she notes that he didn't cry, but later she wonders whether his quiet means he is not really fine.

grounding: A toddler ignores his mother's leaving and turns away when hurt, and his grandmother begins to suspect his calm hides stress.

subtype: Toddler who does not seek comfort [Actor]
passage: Toddler Room note, by Simran. Chetan, two, waved his father off this morning without a glance. At ten he fell off the low slide and scraped his knee. No tears. He walked to the corner, turned his back and held his knee, breathing fast. When I came close, he shuffled away. I sat nearby and said, "That hurt. I'm right here." After a while he leaned on my arm. Plan: stay close in hard moments; tell his father at pickup.

qa.q: What happened to Chetan at ten?
qa.a: He fell off the low slide and scraped his knee.

qa.q: What does Chetan's fast breathing in the corner suggest?
qa.a: It suggests he is stressed and hurting, even though he does not cry or ask for comfort.

qa.q: What did Simran choose to do when Chetan shuffled away, and why did it help?
qa.a: Simran sat nearby, named the hurt and stayed available without grabbing him, so he could come close on his own.

qa.q: How might Chetan's father feel hearing about today at pickup?
qa.a: He may be surprised, since Chetan seemed so unbothered at drop-off, and it could help him notice the hidden stress.

grounding: A caregiver notes a toddler who seems unbothered at parting and turns away when hurt, and stays close until he leans in.
